findings: Decode is not attention-bound. gemma4_attention_decode_class_kernel is 50.04 ms, 1.6% of the 3067.9 ms total, so the 2X decode target has to come out of the expert matmuls and the activation packing, which together are about 71%.

The single largest line is the Q4_K MoE gate/up at 860.49 ms, 28.0%, in 1827 calls - 28.5 per decode step, one per layer. The Q5_1 expert down is next at 530.48 ms, 17.3%, also 1827 calls, and it runs a selected-GEMV kernel as expected for decode.

Activation packing is the surprise: gguf_k_pack8_prefill_out_kernel appears twice, at 576.92 ms in 12915 calls and 222.23 ms in 64 calls, together 26.0% of decode. The 12915 is 202 launches per decode step, which at 44.7 us per launch means decode is spending a quarter of its time in a large number of very small packing launches. Reducing the launch count is therefore a candidate lever in its own right, separate from making any single kernel faster.

The 'prefill' in those kernel names is historical, not a routing error. gemma4_moe_prefill_route_enabled requires lanes >= _PREFILL_MIN_LANES_PER_EXPERT * num_experts, and decode has lanes = 1 * top_k = 8 against 128 experts, so the row-reusing prefill route is correctly off and the selected/GEMV family is what runs. I checked this because 54% of decode time sits in kernels named prefill, and the names alone would have read as a mis-dispatch.

The 202-per-step packing launch count is now explained. The kernel lives in gguf_q8_0_pack8_gemv.py, whose docstring calls it 'the decode-shaped' kernel, so it is the q8_0 dense decode GEMV and the 'prefill' in its name is historical. 12915 calls over 64 steps and 29 layers is 7 per layer, which is the seven dense projections - q, k, v, o, gate, up, down. Each is a separate launch because each has its own weight matrix, so this is not a batching oversight; the lever is the per-launch cost and the kernel's own efficiency at the decode shape, not a reduction in launch count by combining unrelated projections.
limits: One prompt length, one output length, one box, one profiling run. Decode cost varies with context length - the earlier length curve showed decode falling from 21.91 to 19.57 tok/s between 128 and 2048 prompt tokens - so this profile describes a 128-token context.
Kernel time is not a promotion claim. This sizes the next unit.
